title: Decided to upload my game to itch while polishing my assets
author: son_o_gong
selftext:
I’ve just realized how easy-peasy it is to upload a game to [itch.io](https://antonio-ingegnere.itch.io/road-delivery-service), so… why not?

Just a heads-up: this is a super-duper early technical pre-alpha—or whatever you want to call it. Most of the core mechanics are already in place, but the story, proper menus, and general polish are still missing. Very much a work in progress.

It’s playable on mobile, but the desktop browser experience is much better. Use the arrow keys to drive and press Esc to adjust the settings.

By default the car settings are very bad, so if you want to get better driving experience adjust it in menu then (Esc button for menu).

comments.author: fisj
comments.body: As it stands this post breaks rule 1. Can you give details on how you used AI in development? This isnt the "game promotion" sub. Its for development discussion. If you're gonna show off your game you need to wrap it in the context of development, to other developers.

replies.author: son_o_gong
replies.body:
Thank you for the comment and I understand your concern. So, the initial post was done some days ago - [https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1trbwpo/almost\_100\_ai\_generated/](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1trbwpo/almost_100_ai_generated/) and this one is just a follow up.

As for the toolset:Claude for code in Godot, and ChatGPT, Aseprite, and several custom tools built with Claude’s assistance for asset creation. I also occasionally use [pixellab.ai](http://pixellab.ai) for animations.

The project is clearly marked on [itch.io](http://itch.io) as containing AI-generated content.

I’d also appreciate some clarification on how these rules are expected to be applied across similar posts, so I can make sure future updates fully comply.

replies.author: fisj
replies.body: Every post must adhere to the rules, in isolation. It doesnt matter if previous posts covered actual development details. Mods cannot be expected to "keep track".
